There are both pluses and minuses for the Panda.

On the plus side: It actually holds of a lot (I wash dishcloths/cleaning cloths in it); it's got a separate spin function, which does a nice job; and once you figure out the instructions, it's easy to use. There's also a lint catcher, which is fairly easy to unscrew and clean out.

There are a few minuses: First, the instructions are non-intuitive and unclear. For example, they'll say, "drain the washer," but won't explain until two pages later HOW to drain it. If you've used a machine like this before, I suppose it'd be obvious, but as a first-time user, I kept making notes and drawing arrows to show how the process related to the instruction to do something. Second: the hose worked well the first few times I used it, but the connection to the faucet is very fragile, and now I have to hold it in place when I fill the washer, or it comes unattached. (If it comes unattached while I'm washing something, I'm done with the Panda). Additionally, the marker for the timer is indistinguishable from the other markers, which makes it really tough to figure out both how much time you've set it for, and whether it's the cycle is finished or merely pausing. It also doesn't drain fully. I'd say it drains 98.5% of the water, but that 1.5% is enough that you have to let it air dry between washes. For about a month, this Panda washing machine was a great item! It could handle all of my clothes (jeans, sweaters, etc.), both wash and spin dry. The clothes were dry enough after spin to hang on a clothesline without dripping, and were completely wearable the next day -- perfect!

However, after a short period of time, the Panda started leaking from the bottom. My fix was placing the Panda in the bathtub and leaving the faucet running for the duration of the wash cycle -- a nuisance, but workable. Then, I noticed that my clothes weren't being washed quite as vigorously as before. Underclothes were coming out still dirty, and the drained water was clearer, reflecting a lack of cleaning. Unfortunately, I had to downgrade its role in my clothes-washing routine, as it just wasn't cleaning clothes well anymore.

This Panda is good for extremely small, infrequent loads; I'm going to continue using it for dirty running clothes, since I'd rather handle the annoyances of the machine than deal with the smell. However, it's not a suitable replacement for washing all clothes on a regular basis, as I was hoping.

Procedure:
WASH: fill washer with included hose or faucet sprayer. Add detergent and clothes, run for desired amount of time (max 10 mins). Drain with drainage hose. Repeat if desired.
RINSE: Refill with clean water, run for desired amount of time again (max 10 mins). Drain. Repeat if desired.
You can then spin clothes individually or in small batches using spin basket. Removes most excess water, but time consuming.

2. Wash cycle is quiet.
3. You can put a good amount of items in there to wash.
4. Good agitation for a small machine.
5. You can put it on your countertop...it's compact enough. And I have MINIMAL counter space.

CONS:
1. When using spin basket in spin cycle, it REALLY moves around. I had to hold it down to stop it from moving about. So, I have to figure out out to secure it so it doesn't move much or at all.
